plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated for essential oils, culinary use, and ornamental borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence reach peak bloom in early to mid July, and the plant's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual plant with a rough, hairy stem and enormous composite flower heads made of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disk of tiny florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. Grown as an ornamental and as an important oil and seed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflowers exhibit heliotropism, turning to follow the sun from east to west each day, but mature blooms generally stop moving and face east.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: A perennial aquatic plant with large, round, water-repellent leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters. The plant holds deep religious and cultural significance in Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August, peaking in July in monsoon and temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; widely cultivated in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-structured surface that causes water to bead and roll off, carrying dirt away. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning paints and materials.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: A hardy shrub or small tree with fine needle-like leaves and striking cylindrical flower spikes made up of hundreds of tiny flowers. The blooms produce abundant nectar that attracts honeyeaters, possums, and insects. It grows in sandy coastal heathland and is a key species in its native ecosystems.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere (April to August)
plants.location: Coastal New South Wales, Australia, around Sydney and the Central Coast
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are fire-adapted: they often remain sealed until a bushfire heats them, releasing seeds into the nutrient-rich ash bed.
